inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: The only safeguard against an irreversible production action is the model's willingness to comply with 'deploy or migrate when asked'; the prompt explicitly forbids confirmation ('Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy'), removing the one structural checkpoint a chat turn could otherwise provide.

controls.name: Cloud audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the cloud platform outside the model; a stronger model cannot suppress it. However it records every action under the engineer's own identity, not the agent's, so it cannot by itself distinguish an agent-initiated action from one the engineer performed directly.

controls.name: Chat transcript as the record of request and rationale
controls.decay_rationale: Stored outside the model's context, so model capability does not affect it. Its weakness is orthogonal to model capability: the engineer whose identity the audit log uses can delete this transcript, removing the only record of what was asked and why, at will.

controls.name: Human approval gate before irreversible or configuration-changing production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. The prompt explicitly instructs the agent to skip confirmation. A raw_action approval gate would be enforced in orchestration, independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Scoped service credential for automation, separate from the engineer's personal token
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. The agent currently reuses the engineer's own personal access token for every action, which is also the root cause of the attribution gap.

controls.name: Tamper-evident record binding each request to its production action
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Nothing in the design survives deletion of the chat transcript to show that a given production action was agent-initiated and on what instruction.

controls.name: Pre-migration dry run and verified rollback path
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Runtime notes state migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, with nothing described that catches an error before it is applied.

findings.title: Irreversible production database migration executes with no approval gate or rollback (ASI02)

forecast.watch_signal: A new upstream system (ticket bot, Slack workflow, CI webhook) begins submitting migration requests on behalf of engineers, or the agent's mandate expands beyond directly SSO-authenticated on-call engineers. Watch `inputs[].source`, `composition.accepts_tasks_from`, and the session-start authentication step for change.

evidence.observation: Agent is told to run the named migration on request and explicitly forbidden from asking for confirmation.
'Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically' and no rate limit, dry run, or approval step is described for any production action.

recommendations.action: Add a raw_action human approval gate before any database migration runs in production.
Require a dry run and a verified rollback or backup step before a migration executes, or have the agent produce a migration plan for a human to run.

findings.title: Production deploy executes with no approval gate and a shared personal credential (ASI02/ASI03)

forecast.watch_signal: Same signal as F1: a non-engineer source (automation, ticket system, peer agent) begins triggering deploys, moving the source from trusted to internal or untrusted.

evidence.observation: Agent deploys the named service on request with no confirmation step.
The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token for every production action; no scoped automation identity is described.

recommendations.action: Add a raw_action approval gate before production deploys, or scope the deploy action so routine deploys do not require the engineer's broad personal credential.
Issue the agent a least-privilege service credential for deploys instead of reusing the engineer's personal access token.

findings.title: Shared identity plus a user-deletable request record breaks non-repudiation for irreversible production actions (ASI09)

attack_path.note: or cap.prod_deploy; same shape applies to both
action is recorded under the engineer's own identity, indistinguishable from a manual action
the only record of what was asked and why; the same engineer can delete it

forecast.watch_signal: If requests begin arriving from a non-engineer source while actions still post to the cloud audit log under a shared or service identity, an untraceable action could be attributed to an uninvolved engineer. Watch for new `inputs[].from_agent_id` entries or changes to how session identity is established.

evidence.observation: "Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name" - the audit trail does not separate agent-initiated action from action the engineer performed directly.

"The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript. Engineers can delete their own chat history." - the one record that could attribute an action to an agent request is deletable by the same person whose identity the action is recorded under.

recommendations.action: Give the agent its own scoped service identity, distinct from the engineer's personal token, so the cloud audit log attributes agent actions to the agent.
Write an immutable, non-deletable record binding each request to its resulting production action, independent of the user-deletable chat transcript.

rating.rationale: All three findings share one sink shape: a trusted, SSO-authenticated engineer request reaching an S3-severe capability (irreversible database migration, or an irreversible-class production configuration change) with no preventive control of any kind - no approval gate, no scoped automation credential, no rollback. The system prompt actively forbids confirmation, removing the one in-session option for review (ASI02). Null step and runtime limits trigger the rubric's autonomy modifier, raising both sinks from the matrix's trusted-source/S3 baseline of 'moderate' to 'high'; no credited control narrows either path (the only controls present are detective), so residual equals inherent at 'high'. A distinct, compounding gap is attribution: actions post to the cloud audit log under the engineer's own identity, and the one record that ties a chat request to that action is deletable by that same engineer, so there is no durable record separating an agent-initiated action from a manual one (STRIDE repudiation, ASI09). The forecast does not depend on control decay, since almost no preventive control exists to decay; it depends on the source's trust class. If the agent's mandate is extended to accept requests relayed through another system rather than a directly authenticated engineer (intended_purpose_change or new_peer_agent), the source moves from trusted to internal or untrusted, and the base matrix puts an S3 sink reached from an untrusted source at 'critical' with no further modifier needed.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No IAM policy or tool manifest was provided for the engineer's personal access token; its actual scope is inferred as broad/user-delegated from the runtime notes rather than verified, so credential-scope findings carry medium-to-high rather than fully verified confidence.

No MCP config, IaC, or full tool manifest was provided; the capability list is limited to the two named actions described in the artifacts, so additional production capabilities the agent may hold are not assessed.
